question: Q-013
reason: Read the migration and the tracing test. The migration is exactly GRANT UPDATE (review_profile) ON TABLE ursitoare.tenant TO ursitoare_app; no other migration grants the app role more than SELECT on tenant. The tenant table has RLS with the tenant_isolation policy and a CHECK on review_profile, which explain the 0-row cross-tenant update and the 23514 for bogus. The test asserts every WHEN and THEN element of the scenario with the exact SQLSTATEs, the tenant B profile, and the empty violations list; the report shows it passed with a red assertion failure.

checked.quote: GRANT UPDATE (review_profile) ON TABLE ursitoare.tenant TO ursitoare_app;
checked.claim: The migration grants the app role exactly the review_profile column update, as the requirement and the design data model demand.

checked.quote: review_profile text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'solo' CHECK (review_profile IN ('solo', 'team'))
checked.claim: A check constraint on review_profile makes the value bogus fail with SQLSTATE 23514.
Row-level security on the tenant table limits the app role's update to its own tenant's row, so the update aimed at tenant_b changes 0 rows.

checked.quote: GRANT SELECT ON TABLE ursitoare.tenant TO ursitoare_app;
checked.claim: Before migration 180 the app role held only SELECT on tenant, so name updates, INSERT and DELETE are refused with 42501.
The test first asserts the ledger row version 180 and, on the next line, the name admin_api.
